messages:
ashley: heads up — customer (Acme Mobile) hitting repeated SSE disconnects mid-stream when phone swaps from 5G -> WiFi. app v2.4.1 on Pixel 6. They see partial JSON payloads and the client doesn't auto-reconnect. Can someone triage? :thinking_face:

support-bot: ticket #34211 created and linked to this thread. severity=P2. Correlation: cor-id=acme-34211

eli: can you paste a minimal client log and the partial payload they get? also which EventSource polyfill / native API are they using?

ashley: pasted a scrubbed log from the customer (timestamps removed). small snippet below — they hit this after ~9s into the stream when switching networks:

```
I/StreamClient: open SSE conn -> /v1/streams?model=gpt-small
I/Network: link-change: CELLULAR->WIFI rssi:-78->-92
W/SSE: recv partial chunk: '{"choices":[{"delta":{"text":"Hello wor'
E/SSE: connection closed by remote (code=1006)
I/StreamClient: reconnect attempt 1 (backoff jitter)
I/StreamClient: client didn't reassemble partial payload; UI shows truncated text
```

ashley: example partial payload they received: `{"choices":[{"delta":{"text":"Hello wor"}, ...` (truncated mid-token).

miguel: this looks like a classic RSSI dip + TCP half-close during network handoff. a few quick checks:
- confirm client is using EventSource polyfill vs native; polyfills often don't handle `onerror`->auto-reconnect well on android webviews.
- verify keepalive/comments from server (we send `:keepalive\n\n` every 15s?). if network flap > RTT then TCP might drop before next keepalive.
- check client's reconnect/jitter logic: are they reissuing the same `Last-Event-ID` or doing full restart?

miguel: repro steps i want to try locally:
1) Pixel 6 on Android 13, mobile data -> force WiFi attach with weak AP (rssi ~ -90).
2) Start SSE stream via curl or app.
3) toggle airplane-mode quick (simulate NAT/IP change).
4) observe partial chunk then RST/1006.

jamie: also check token refresh timing — if the client requests a new token on reconnect and takes >3s the backend may reject or the client may open a new stream without reusing stream id. which library is the app using for streaming? is it `EventSource` native or a `fetch`-based polyfill?

ashley: they're using a small in-house polyfill (not native). header they send on connect: `Authorization: Bearer <short-lived>` with `x-redwood-cid: acme-34211`. token ttl=60s. they refresh at 45s.

eli: token ttl=60s + refresh at 45s is risky if network flap causes reconnect around refresh time. can we confirm whether the partial occurs near token refresh? but logs above show 9s in so probably different.

miguel: short-term workaround for customer: bump client-side reconnect backoff to do immediate short retries AND enable reassembly of partial chunks client-side (buffer until SSE event boundary) — many clients treat any receive-close as fatal and drop partial buffer. Also, server-side: enable comment heartbeats every 10s and reduce idle TTL for mobile connections. Example server heartbeat ping line we recommend:

```
: heartbeat\n\n
```

jamie: server/team note — we currently send comments every 15s. mobile handoffs sometimes need 8-12s. Can infra lower to 10s for the mobile pool? tagging eng-runtime. :eyes:

oncall: i'll pick this up for next triage window at 11:00 PDT. add me if you need packet captures.

ashley: customer supplied the partial payload they saw and the x-redwood-cid above. full sample (scrubbed):

```
{"event":"response.delta","data":"{\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"text\":\"Hello wor\"}}]}"}
```

eli: can you ask them to attach adb logcat + `tcpdump` pcap when they reproduce? instructions: on device `adb shell tcpdump -w /sdcard/sse.pcap host api.redwood.example.com` then pull. also capture `dumpsys connectivity` and connectivity manager states. this helps check MTU/rapid ip change/RST.

ashley: will request pcap + `dumpsys` and share. customer is ok to try repro tomorrow.

miguel: one more server-side idea: if the runtime detects a mid-stream client re-open with same `x-redwood-cid` within short window, attempt to stitch last known kv-cache and partial payload to reduce visible truncation. requires a short buffer window but could hide mid-network flips for friendly clients. not a quick fix but filing RFC.

jamie: also confirm client uses `withCredentials` false/true and whether TLS session resumption is broken by some carriers. sometimes TLS renegotiation + NAT leads to 1006.

oncall: action items:
- ashley: get pcap + adb logs + exact device repro steps from customer (ETA tomorrow)
- miguel/eli: try local repro with Pixel 6 + weak AP and capture server side logs
- jamie: check keepalive window and token-refresh race on reconnect paths

ashley: noted and will update ticket #34211 when I have captures. thanks all :pray:

eli: thanks — ping here once uploads are in and we'll triage live.
